premise.statement: Dark matter is partly the projected cause and partly the projected effect of higher-dimensional gravitational shear structure; those shear bands form the underlying universal terrain used by advanced Black Light transit mathematics.
safeguards: Do not equate the premise with one exclusive real-world dark-matter particle model.
Do not claim that all dark matter is exclusively higher-dimensional shear.
Do not treat gravitational lensing as an illusion; projected terrain produces real 3+1D gravitational effects.
Do not treat terrain as static.
Do not make every transit family interact with terrain identically.
Do not infer chronology violation from higher-dimensional terrain.

observationModel.epochRule: Every route solution using terrain inference MUST retain the terrain model epoch and uncertainty/covariance state.

sharedRouteModel.rule: For discontinuous families D_f is a generalized transition cost, not necessarily traversed metric length. distanceModelType must remain explicit.

generatorRules: All true FTL families consume the shared terrain model as an environmental/reference input even when terrain is not their primary operator.
The inertial-torch family consumes the effective gravitational terrain for navigation only and receives no FTL route-gain term.
Terrain state must retain model epoch and uncertainty; stale but numerically precise solutions are invalid.
Higher Path capability may result from improved terrain mathematics, field coupling, materials, structure, navigation, control, recovery, or energy efficiency rather than gross power alone.
Family-specific equations remain authoritative over the shared terrain layer when defining what the drive actually does.
Uncalibrated terrain constants remain PROPOSED and must not be emitted as recovered setting constants.
